name: spear_hew3

authoring.method: hand-keyed technique rows over the pilot's pipeline (F-curves on control properties, FK in the runtime overlay's arithmetic, two-bone arm and leg solves); the palms' and the shaft's geometry through the stroke is re-timed from the previous clips (named in the docs); no motion capture, no video-to-motion

axes: skeleton space, Z up. Stance frame: right = left thigh to right thigh (flat), front = up x right. Turn: yaw positive toward the character's left (about up), pitch about the stance right (positive tips a standing segment back), roll about the stance front (positive tips it to the right); composed yaw, pitch, roll about the bone's own origin. Aim: azimuth from the stance front toward its right, elevation above the horizontal (absolute). Move/Foot: forward, right, up metres in the stance frame.

rest_pose.note: the base stance the keys lie over (hips 71 degrees right of the facing); the carry squares the hips with a pelvis yaw of 71 degrees (WeaponPoseClip.SquareYaw) so the clips start and end on that; a bone with no track at the skeleton's reference pose

timing.source: the hammer's strike at the spear's tempo 0.85 (docs/claw-spear-animations.md section 2); length, hit and combo opening are the strike's

technique: Light hew 3: the flat horizontal cut at waist height from behind the right side round to far left, a pivoting step turning the whole body through it. Source technique: the horizontal cut of Meyer's Zwerchhau family as it is applied to the halberd, struck from a step and a pivot. Pass 4: a more compact coil, a higher-power acceleration into the hit and a carry-through of the hips after it.
